facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman
history of systemic lupus erythematosus
fever
Temperature of 101.5°F
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Normocytic anemia (mean corpuscular volume: 99 fL; hemoglobin: 11.7 g/dL; hematocrit: 33.4%)
Platelet count: 81 K/μL (thrombocytopenia)
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:1280 (speckled pattern)
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
Dusky malar erythema with focal heme crusting

concepts.why: The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with fever, erythematous plaques, and a high antinuclear antibody titer.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and target lesions, consistent with acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a low platelet count, indicating thrombocytopenia.
The patient has a low hemoglobin level and a normal mean corpuscular volume, indicating normocytic anemia.
The patient presents with bullae and target lesions, which may be indicative of vasculitis.
The patient presents with bullae and a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, consistent with bullous lupus erythematosus.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and target lesions, consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with a high antinuclear antibody titer, which may be indicative of lupus nephritis.
The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with thrombocytopenia, which may be indicative of antiphospholipid syndrome.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and target lesions, consistent with neonatal lupus erythematosus.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face and numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers, are consistent with Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus. The presence of bullae also supports the consideration of Bullous Lupus Erythematosus as a runner-up.
